issues.description: State-machine collapse of working/walking into one label is undocumented and the DFS invariant is not stated.
issues.detail: The patch merges two distinct DFS phases into a single 'walking' label that push() still reads for cycle detection. No comment states the invariant (a 'walking' node is on the stack with children pushed but not yet drained) or proves the cycle-detection branch still holds. Write the invariant down or split the states back out.

issues.description: Behavioral change: s.state[k] = sorted now only runs when yield returns true, silently altering the loop postcondition.
issues.detail: Previously the sorted marker was set unconditionally after pop; now it is skipped on early yield=false termination. The deferred clear papers over this for the current API but couples correctness to defer ordering across distant lines. The commit message does not acknowledge it. Document the postcondition or restore the unconditional assignment.

issues.description: Cleanup-on-defer changes Sorter lifetime contract without documenting reuse, reentrancy, or abandoned-iterator semantics.
issues.detail: Moving clear(state) and stack truncation into defer shifts reset from Sort entry to iterator completion. If the returned iter.Seq is never invoked, or a reentrant-call panic fires before the defer is installed, state from a prior run persists. State the precondition and reuse contract on the Sorter type explicitly rather than relying on the defer as proof.

issues.description: No regression test for the state-reuse bug the PR claims to fix.
issues.detail: The PR title says 'Fix state reuse' but no test calls Sort twice on the same Sorter and asserts the second result, nor asserts len(stack)==0 and len(state)==0 after iteration. A three-line regression test would lock in the contract the defer now establishes and prevent silent reintroduction.

issues.description: Updated comment contains typos ('visisted', 'if its') in the load-bearing state-machine explanation.
issues.detail: The rewritten comment is now the canonical description of the two-visit DFS state model and contains 'visisted' (should be 'visited') and 'if its' (should be 'it's'). Since the state machine just lost a state, this comment carries more explanatory load than before and deserves a clean pass.

issues.description: clear(s.stack) followed by s.stack[:0] fixes a real no-op bug but lacks a one-line comment explaining intent.
issues.detail: The previous s.stack = s.stack[0:] was a no-op that retained stale Node references and prevented GC. The new clear()+reslice pair is correct, but the code does not say why clear precedes truncate (zeroing pointer elements for GC, then dropping length). One line of comment would make the intent legible.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes two real defects (the s.stack[0:] no-op that retained stale Node references, and clobbered/leaked state across Sorter reuse) and that collapsing working/walking is the right direction. However, the change is presented as a cleanup while making three coupled behavioral shifts: state-machine collapse, cleanup moved into defer, and conditional sorted-marker assignment. None of these are documented with an invariant, precondition, or regression test. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — write down the DFS invariant and Sorter reuse contract, add a Sort-twice regression test, fix the comment typos, and the change lands.
